messages:
maria: heads-up — proposing a 'silent fallback window' for A->B releases. idea: after we start routing pilot traffic (5-10%), keep a decision horizon of 10m where we collect metrics but do not alert downstream teams unless auto-rollback triggers. want thoughts on signal freshness and operator UX.

alex: tl;dr: sounds useful. main q: how do we decide the horizon length? 10m seems arbitrary.

jun: agree w/ alex. also we need to be explicit about which metrics count (latency p95, error rate, model-quality QA). otherwise noisy signals will flip us.

maria: good point. current thinking: configurable per-release policy. default horizon = 10m, min 2m, max 60m. signals: p95 latency, 5xx rate, embedding-cosine drift > 0.12 (on eval set).

lia: how do we compute "embedding-cosine drift" in realtime? do we maintain a sliding eval set? that's expensive.

jun: proposal: use a small fixed probe set (50 items) sampled from production mirrors. run inference on both variants and compute mean cosine. cheap enough and gives fast signal.

kate_sre: need to call out observability lag. our metrics pipeline has ~30–90s lag for p95 depending on shard. decision horizon must consider that, otherwise auto-rollback will react to late-arriving spikes.

alex: +1 on lag. also we should include a staleness check: only consider windows where >80% of expected datapoints arrived. otherwise treat as inconclusive and extend horizon or escalate.

maria: nice. here's an example rollout policy snippet I'm thinking of: 
```yaml
policy: 
  pilot_pct: 5
  decision_horizon: 10m
  signals:
    - name: p95_latency
      cmp: increase_pct
      threshold: 25
    - name: error_rate_5xx
      cmp: absolute
      threshold: 0.005
    - name: embed_drift
      cmp: absolute
      threshold: 0.12
  staleness_threshold: 80%
  on_inconclusive: extend_horizon: true
  on_violation: auto_rollback: true
```

lia: question: who owns the on_violation decision? auto_rollback true is scary for product teams. need an override flag per-team and a controlled opt-in.

maria: yep — default should be auto_rollback=false for prod tenants unless gated. internal infra-owned releases can opt into auto_rollback=true. we'll expose the flag in console and API.

kate_sre: ops note: add a cooldown window after rollback to avoid flip-flopping (eg 30m) and include an operator-visible rationale in the event timeline. deploy-bot should annotate the rollback with the triggering signal and raw numbers.

alex: infra boundary question: should decision horizon logic live inside the rollout controller or as a separate 'decision-horizon service' that aggregates signals and emits pass/fail?

jun: I vote service. separation keeps rollout controller lightweight and lets us reuse the signal aggregator for experiments and canary dashboards. also easier to swap models of statistical testing.

lia: service requires API contract. minimal contract: start_observation(run_id, variant_ids, signal_set, window); poll_status(run_id) -> {status, reason, raw_signals}. keep it simple.

maria: agreed on service + contract. long-term refactor note: we could push more analysis into a 'statistical engine' that supports sequential tests (e.g., Bayesian AB) to reduce false positives while allowing shorter horizons.

kate_sre: incremental approach: 1) implement basic windowed aggregator with staleness guard and cooldowns, 2) add opt-in auto_rollback for internal tenants, 3) evolve to sequential testing. that gives ops time to tune thresholds.

alex: small UX ask: console should show a live decision timer and an estimated completion time (accounting for staleness). also a single-button abort that immediately pins traffic back.

deploy-bot: deployment 7234: pilot rollout started for release/infra-opt. routing 5% to v2. decision_horizon=10m.

maria: thanks, all. action items: alex to draft API contract + console mock, jun to prototype probe runner for embed drift, kate to add cooldown and deploy-bot annotation changes, lia to write opt-in policy text. I'll collate and create an RFC draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

alex: will do.

jun: prototyping now.

lia: writing doc.

kate_sre: logging followups in oncall runbook.

maria: closing loop — if anyone wants to be on RFC ping me.
